title: Eleven Pounds and One Receipt
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：cost　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cost 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 my father ① counted the cost of a repair that had taken eleven weekends, and he said the counting was the whole of the deciding. The ② cost, meaning the price and not the time, came to eleven pounds and stayed that figure; cost, he said, is the only thing in a repair that is judged by how early it is counted.

Every ③ cost in that house had the same receipt, and the ④ cost at the end, meaning the one he had not counted and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever argued about twice. Cost, my mother said, is nine parts receipt and one part somebody willing to count; my father said the counting is the part that fills the weekend.

My grandmother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the cost was the whole of the victory, meaning the loss and not the price. The ⑥ cost, meaning the loss and not any of that, is the only thing in a victory that everybody pays and nobody puts on a receipt; cost, she said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a price and a loss. He said the loss is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ cost had become a line in an estimate, and the estimate had become an argument about the receipt. The ⑧ cost of the whole thing, my father wrote in March, was one repair and thirty years of counting; cost, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to count. She said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cost I remember is the one at the end, which fell due in 1981 and is still described as the heaviest in the county. A ⑩ cost, my mother said in 1983, is the only thing that improves by being counted; every cost, she said, is a loss that has agreed to look like a price. She said the loss was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 费用（指那个价钱本身，与那些时间相对）
C. 固定搭配：count the cost of 计算……的代价
D. n. 费用（指那栋房子里每一笔）
E. n. 代价（指末尾那一笔）
F. n. 代价；损失（抽象：胜利付出的代价）
G. n. 费用（指估价单里提到的那一笔）
H. n. 成本；代价（抽象总称）

items.q: counted the cost of a repair that had taken eleven weekends
The cost, meaning the price and not the time
the cost was the whole of the victory
the cost had become a line in an estimate
The cost of the whole thing
A cost, my mother said in 1983

answers.why: count the cost of 意为“计算……的代价”，1967 年父亲计算了一次花了十一个周末的修理的代价。
cost 意为“费用”，指那个价钱本身而不是那些时间，算下来是十一英镑。
cost 指那栋房子里每一笔费用，每一笔都有同样的收据。
cost 指末尾那一笔（他没算进去的那一笔），是唯一有人争论过两次的。
cost 意为“代价、损失”，祖母说代价就是那场胜利的全部，指的是付出的损失而不是那个价钱。
cost 为抽象用法，指胜利付出的代价而不是那个价钱，是胜利里人人都付了、却无人开收据的东西。
cost 意为“费用”，指估价单里提到的那一笔，到 1975 年这笔费用成了估价单里的一行。
cost 意为“成本、代价”，父亲三月写道，整件事的代价是一次修理三十年的计算。
cost 意为“费用、成本”，我记得的是末尾那一笔，1981 年到期，至今仍被说成全县最重的。
cost 为抽象总称，母亲说一笔代价是唯一会因为被计算而变好的东西。
